From: markus.klein@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler: Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for taking time today — good call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Key requirements you called out:
- Target steady-state throughput: ~300 inference TPS for our 2 core products (peak 450 TPS)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 150ms for completion on typical prompts (~250 tokens)
- Availability/regulatory: 99.9% SLA, EU data residency for some customers, SOC2 + KMS integration
- Cost sensitivity: goal is unit cost < $0.0007/token for production traffic

What Redwood brings (high level):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed capacity guarantees and configurable autoscale/burst policies
- Smart routing & fallback: can route to cheaper model variants or hosted fallback if Dedicated capacity is constrained
- Cost controls: batching/caching, quantization guidance, and per-route cost observability
- Security/compliance: Private deployments with KMS/HSM support and audit logs (we'll provide SOC2 artifacts)

Competitive notes vs hyperscalers (summary):
- Hyperscalers: broad availability but often shared noisy neighbors unless you do expensive reserved instances; pricing transparency and fine-grained observability tend to be weaker for inference workloads
- Redwood Dedicated: predictable performance and cost at production scale, and simplified rollout/rollback tools specific to LLM serving

Proposed next steps:
1) We run a short perf comparison: baseline on your preferred hyperscaler instance (tell us the exact SKU you want tested) vs Redwood Dedicated using an equivalent GPU config. We'll measure p95/p99 latencies, sustained TPS, and cost per token.
2) You share a 24-72 hour sample traffic trace + representative prompt sets and any privacy constraints.
3) We scope a 2-week POC (reserved pool) — we'll provide a test plan and pricing estimate for reserved capacity.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-one-pager.pdf (overview), POC-Test-Plan.xlsx (template).

Available times for a 30-min follow-up to finalize the POC scope: Tue/Wed next week (07/14-07/15) morning PT.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
